results.name: rule_far_extension_large_minus_pair
results.description: For sets whose examples all share a multiples-of-m rule (m 3-12, or m=2 with no larger m) or a common final digit, yes-rate on rule-consistent non-example targets 10+ outside the span for 3-4-example sets minus 2-example sets; observed above null_mean means rules overtake ranges with more examples faster than the model predicts (below = slower).

results.name: participant_far_generalization_sd
results.description: SD across participants (new participant at each trial_index reset) of the yes-rate on non-example targets 10+ outside the examples' span, after subtracting the mean of the participant's design batch (5 consecutive participants); observed above null_mean means individuals differ in generalization breadth beyond what the single-population model allows.
results.code:
# name: participant_far_generalization_sd
# description: SD across participants (new participant at each trial_index reset) of the yes-rate on non-example targets 10+ outside the examples' span, after subtracting the mean of the participant's design batch (5 consecutive participants); observed above null_mean means individuals differ in generalization breadth beyond what the single-population model allows.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[True, ti[1:] <= ti[:-1]]) - 1
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    u = df["number_set"].unique()
    lo = df["number_set"].map({s: min(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u}).to_numpy()
    hi = df["number_set"].map({s: max(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u}).to_numpy()
    far = (t <= lo - 10) | (t >= hi + 10)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    if far.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    rates = pd.Series(r[far]).groupby(pid[far]).mean()
    batch = rates.index.to_numpy() // 5
    dev = rates.to_numpy() - pd.Series(rates.to_numpy()).groupby(batch).transform("mean").to_numpy()
    return float(np.std(dev)) if len(dev) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: shared_tens_digit_out_of_span
results.description: Among non-example targets outside the examples' span, yes-rate for targets sharing a tens digit (same decade, t//10) with some example minus targets sharing none; observed above null_mean means people generalize by decade/surface-digit similarity more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: shared_tens_digit_out_of_span
# description: Among non-example targets outside the examples' span, yes-rate for targets sharing a tens digit (same decade, t//10) with some example minus targets sharing none; observed above null_mean means people generalize by decade/surface-digit similarity more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    u = df["number_set"].unique()
    arr = {s: np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")]) for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].to_numpy()
    ex = np.full((len(df), 4), -1000)
    for s, a in arr.items():
        ex[ns == s, :len(a)] = a
    valid = ex > -1000
    lo = np.where(valid, ex, 1000).min(axis=1); hi = np.where(valid, ex, -1000).max(axis=1)
    isex = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dec = np.where(valid, ex // 10, -99)
    share = (dec == (t // 10)[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    base = ((t < lo) | (t > hi)) & ~isex
    a = base & share; b = base & ~share
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: recency_last_minus_first_example
results.description: Among non-example targets for sets of 2+ examples, yes-rate when the target is closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown one minus yes-rate when closer to the first; observed away from null_mean (model is order-invariant) means presentation order biases generalization (positive = recency).

results.name: within_span_near_minus_far_example
results.description: Among non-example targets strictly inside the examples' span (sets of 2+ examples with span >= 15), yes-rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus yes-rate for targets 8+ from every example; observed above null_mean means people show a similarity gradient inside the span that the flat interval/rule model under-produces.
results.code:
# name: within_span_near_minus_far_example
# description: Among non-example targets strictly inside the examples' span (sets of 2+ examples with span >= 15), yes-rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus yes-rate for targets 8+ from every example; observed above null_mean means people show a similarity gradient inside the span that the flat interval/rule model under-produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    lst = [np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")]) for s in df["number_set"].unique()]
    info = {s: a for s, a in zip(df["number_set"].unique(), lst)}
    ns = df["number_set"].to_numpy()
    lo = np.array([info[s].min() for s in ns]); hi = np.array([info[s].max() for s in ns])
    n = np.array([len(info[s]) for s in ns])
    ex = np.full((len(df), 4), -1000)
    for s, a in info.items():
        ex[ns == s, :len(a)] = a
    dmin = np.abs(ex - t[:, None]).min(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    base = (n >= 2) & (hi - lo >= 15) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & (dmin > 0)
    near = base & (dmin <= 3); far = base & (dmin >= 8)
    if near.sum() == 0 or far.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[near].mean() - r[far].mean())

results.name: wide_minus_narrow_span_inspan_yes
results.description: Among non-example targets inside the span of 3-4-example sets, yes-rate for wide-span sets (span >= 50) minus narrow-span sets (span <= 20); observed below null_mean means people fill in wide spans less than the interval model's flat in-span coverage predicts (above = they fill wide spans more).
results.code:
# name: wide_minus_narrow_span_inspan_yes
# description: Among non-example targets inside the span of 3-4-example sets, yes-rate for wide-span sets (span >= 50) minus narrow-span sets (span <= 20); observed below null_mean means people fill in wide spans less than the interval model's flat in-span coverage predicts (above = they fill wide spans more).
def test_statistic(df):
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    u = df["number_set"].unique()
    lo = df["number_set"].map({s: min(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u}).to_numpy()
    hi = df["number_set"].map({s: max(int(x) for x in s.split(",")) for s in u}).to_numpy()
    n = df["number_set"].map({s: s.count(",") + 1 for s in u}).to_numpy()
    isex = np.array([str(tt) in s.split(",") for s, tt in zip(df["number_set"].to_numpy(), t)])
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    base = (n >= 3) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~isex
    w = base & (hi - lo >= 50); nr = base & (hi - lo <= 20)
    if w.sum() == 0 or nr.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[w].mean() - r[nr].mean())

results.name: round_number_bias_no_round_examples
results.description: For sets containing no multiple of 10, yes-rate on multiple-of-10 targets minus yes-rate on other non-example targets; observed above null_mean means people over-endorse round numbers as a salience bias the rule/range model under-produces.

results.name: same_set_response_perseveration
results.description: Within a participant (trial_index resets) and on consecutive trials with the same number_set, P(yes | previous answer yes) minus P(yes | previous answer no); observed above null_mean means answers carry over trial to trial (perseveration) beyond what the stimulus-driven model produces.
results.code:
# name: same_set_response_perseveration
# description: Within a participant (trial_index resets) and on consecutive trials with the same number_set, P(yes | previous answer yes) minus P(yes | previous answer no); observed above null_mean means answers carry over trial to trial (perseveration) beyond what the stimulus-driven model produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[True, ti[1:] <= ti[:-1]])
    ns = df["number_set"].to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    ok = (pid[1:] == pid[:-1]) & (ns[1:] == ns[:-1])
    prev = r[:-1][ok]; cur = r[1:][ok]
    if (prev == 1).sum() == 0 or (prev == 0).sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(cur[prev == 1].mean() - cur[prev == 0].mean())
